articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft patched 167 vulns including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. Chrome had its fourth zero-day of the year because apparently security is just a suggestion now.

articles.title: Meta U-turns on encryption push for Instagram as DMs go plaintext
articles.summary: The 'Dirty Frag' Linux flaw gives root access with no patches available after disclosure embargo broke. When responsible disclosure goes irresponsibly wrong, admins cry.

articles.title: cPanel, WHM Release Fixes for Three New Vulnerabilities — Patch Now
articles.summary: CVE-2026 lets remote attackers leak Ollama's entire process memory without authentication. 300,000 servers globally just became very uncomfortable with their life choices.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas got owned by data extortionists, disrupting schools nationwide with ransom demands on login pages. Finals week just became exponentially more stressful for millions of students.

articles.title: Congress Narrowed the GUARD Act, But Serious Problems Remain
articles.summary: Russian military hackers mass-harvested Microsoft Office tokens by exploiting old router vulns. Your ancient Linksys just became Moscow's favorite authentication buffet.

articles.title: Big Finance Might Be Dooming the SPLC — Even Before Its Day in Court
articles.summary: DOJ now treats dodging FOIA requests as a crime worthy of arrest and strip searches. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a subpoena.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Linux Rootkit, macOS Crypto Stealer, WebSocket Skimmers and More
articles.summary: Meta abandons Instagram DM encryption, giving itself full visibility into user chats again. Zuckerberg's privacy promises have the lifespan of a mayfly.

articles.title: A manual pentest costs 50,000 dollars. Intruder built an AI that does it in minutes.
articles.summary: The 90-day disclosure window is dead because LLMs compress exploit development to near-zero timeframes. Responsible disclosure just got a machine learning reality check.

articles.title: 'Dirty Frag' Linux flaw one-ups CopyFail with no patches and public root exploit
articles.summary: New worm eliminates competitor malware before taking control itself. Even cybercriminals are practicing hostile takeovers now—capitalism finds a way.
